title: APB3 debug port crosses into CPU domain unsynchronised (GH #95 gate finding)
description:
The GH #95 cdc_snitch gate's only unwaived residue: 233 registers, all one finding.

Top-level apb_* debug ports (apb_paddr_i/psel/penable/pwrite/pwdata) feed u_cpu
directly at soc_top.sv:825-832 with NO synchroniser. GH #93 moved u_cpu onto
cpu_gated_clk, so a chip-boundary bus silently migrated from the fabric domain
into the CPU domain. Affected regs: u_cpu.dbg_pc_wr_data[*], u_cpu.dbg_ctrl_reg[*],
u_cpu.dbg_reg_wr_en, u_cpu.halt_latch_q.

Pre-#93 the implied external contract was 'drive apb_* synchronously to clk_i'.
Post-#93 it silently became 'synchronously to cpu_clk_i'. Nothing documents this.
Multi-bit paddr/pwdata means the failure mode is not just metastability but
incoherent address/data capture.

Compounding: pnr/constraints/phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc:151-155 still asserts the
opposite -- 'the APB3 debug slave sits on apb_interconnect, entirely in the fabric
(sys_clk) domain'. Harmless for timing (line 169 set_false_paths the ports) but the
rationale is now wrong and will mislead.

Options: (a) bridge it with a second apb_cdc_bridge instance, s-face clk_i /
m-face cpu_gated_clk -- restores the pre-#93 contract and makes the SDC true again,
reuses verified IP, debug is an 'infrequent config path' so latency is irrelevant;
(b) declare apb_* a cpu_clk-domain port and fix the SDC rationale + document the
external contract; (c) accepted-risk waiver and defer.

Blocks the GH #95 BAD=0 gate from going green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Test live PMU power-cycle at a divergent cpu_clk/clk ratio (GH #90 residual)
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-08-02 (GH #95). No longer 'untested' -- it is BROKEN.

Test: tb/cocotb/soc/test_soc_pmu_multiclock.py::test_pmu_live_power_cycle
Run:  nix develop --command make -C tb/cocotb/soc soc_pmu_multiclock
Ratio: cpu 3ns / fabric 7ns (coprime). Power-down via real HW path (firmware
programs DMA to write PMU CTRL=MODE_CPU_OFF); power-up via backdoor deposit into
u_soc.u_pmu.u_regbank.regs[0] (a gated CPU cannot re-power itself).

== WHAT WORKS ==
Power-down sequence [0,1,2,3,4] = DOM_ON -> PD_SAVE -> PD_ISO -> PD_GATE -> DOM_OFF.
  Exactly the UPF-mandated order.
OFF steady state: zero CDC-bridge acceptance, zero commits, counter frozen. Correct.
Power-up sequence [5,6,7,8,0] = PU_RST -> ... -> DOM_ON. Exactly the UPF order.
So pmu.sv's sequencer is CORRECT in both directions under divergent-ratio traffic.

== WHAT FAILS ==
After the CPU domain returns to DOM_ON: ZERO commits over 1000 cpu_clk cycles, busy-
loop counter 0 -> 0. The CPU never executes again. Diagnostic trace confirms the
control signals are all correctly restored (cpu_gated_clk_en=1,
pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync=0, pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync=1, cpu_domain_rst_n=1,
pmu_cpu_iso_en_sync=0) -- so this is NOT a stuck clock gate or a stuck clamp.

== MECHANISM (high confidence on the premise, medium on the precise wedge) ==
rv32i_cpu_top uses a SYNCHRONOUS reset (rv32i_cpu_top.sv:327-328: always_ff @(posedge
clk_i) then if (!rst_n_i)), so it needs clock edges WHILE reset is asserted to load
RESET_PC.

commit 30beab3 makes cpu_gated_clk_en = ~pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync.
soc_top.sv:452-470 states the intent verbatim: cpu_gated_clk is 'structurally forbidden
from ticking whenever the CPU-domain-observed PMU reset is asserted ... on power-up, the
gate cannot open until pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync is already 1'. That is deliberate: it
prevents the sync reset from firing and overwriting the retained PC, i.e.
retention-by-construction (docs/POWER_DOMAIN_EVALUATION.md:22,25).

Consequence: on a PMU power cycle the CPU's synchronous reset NEVER fires. The CPU is
therefore REQUIRED to resume from retained state. It does not. Since Phase 5 has no
power switches (retention is a functional no-op, flops hold value), state should survive
-- so something else prevents resumption.

Most likely: the documented no-drain/quiesce gap at soc_top.sv:83-93. The CPU was
mid-AXI-transaction at power-down; async_axi_fifo's reset is a HARD FLUSH, so the
in-flight burst was discarded while the CPU retained its pending request. On resume the
CPU waits forever for a response the bridge has forgotten. NOT yet proven -- needs a
waveform confirming the CPU's stall/valid state at resume.

== DISPOSITION ==
Pre-existing architectural gap, NOT a GH #95 regression. GH #95's test found it, which is
the test doing its job. Do not fix under GH #95. Mark the test expect_fail with a pointer
here so soc_all stays green and the suite alerts when this starts passing.

Fix direction (upstream precedent, from the GH #95 survey): PULP axi_cdc_isolatable +
axi_isolate -- count outstanding transactions, assert isolated_o only at zero, and only
then allow the reset. OpenTitan relies on the same quiescence precondition without
implementing it ('Xbar should not have any outstanding req'). A drain/quiesce step in the
PMU power-down path is the standard answer.
notes:
ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-02 with instrumented evidence. Hypothesis CONFIRMED and sharpened.

EVIDENCE (test_soc_pmu_multiclock, instrumented run):
  At OFF freeze: ic_stall=1, dc_stall=1, all 5 s-face AXI valids=0
  Post-power-up, 60-cycle trace: iso released (pmu_cpu_iso_en_sync=0), ic_stall
  clears at cycle 2, dc_stall STAYS 1 forever, all 5 AXI valids STAY 0.

Reading: the D-cache is not idle and is not requesting. It has already completed
its AR handshake and is blocked waiting for an R-channel response. arvalid=0
because the request phase is done; rvalid=0 because the response no longer exists.

ROOT CAUSE -- a reset-semantics asymmetry:

  u_cpu_axi_cdc.s_rst_n_i = cpu_domain_rst_n         (soc_top.sv:976)
  cpu_domain_rst_n        = cpu_core_rst_n & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync  (:602)

  cdc_reset_sync asserts ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so a PMU CPU power-down HARD-FLUSHES the
  bridge immediately.

  The CPU, by contrast, has a SYNCHRONOUS reset (rv32i_cpu_top.sv:327-328) and its
  clock is gated throughout (commit 30beab3, soc_top.sv:452-470). Its reset
  therefore NEVER FIRES -- deliberately, that is retention-by-construction.

  So 'PMU CPU power-down' means RETAIN to the CPU and FLUSH to the CDC bridge. On
  resume the CPU is still waiting for a response the bridge has forgotten.
  Permanent deadlock. Nothing to do with the PMU sequencer, which is correct.

PROPOSED FIXES:

A. Retention-consistent bridge reset (~1 line). Wire u_cpu_axi_cdc.s_rst_n_i to
   cpu_core_rst_n (the true POR+PLL reset) instead of cpu_domain_rst_n, so the
   bridge retains exactly like the CPU it serves. During OFF the fabric side keeps
   running and completes in-flight transactions into the R FIFO; the ISO clamp holds
   rready=0 so nothing is consumed; on resume the CPU finds its response waiting.
   No drain needed.
   MUST VERIFY FIRST: R-FIFO DEPTH >= max beats outstanding (16B line = 4 beats;
   elaboration guard already forces DEPTH power-of-two >= 4, so it is exactly at
   capacity -- confirm no path allows more). Also confirm the cache arbiter really
   permits only one outstanding refill.
   Caveat: breaks if Phase 6 adds real power switches, since retention stops being
   free -- but that needs retention registers anyway.

B. Drain/quiesce before power-down (correct, matches upstream). PULP
   axi_cdc_isolatable + axi_isolate: count outstanding transactions, assert
   isolated_o only at zero, and only then allow iso/gate/reset. OpenTitan assumes
   the same quiescence precondition without implementing it. This ALSO closes the
   broader pre-existing hazard at soc_top.sv:83-93 (mid-burst CPU reset wedging a
   crossbar slave engine), which fix A does not. Cost: new outstanding-counter +
   isolate FSM, a new pre-PD_SAVE PMU phase, full re-verification.

C. Abandon retention -- ungate the clock during reset so the CPU reboots from
   RESET_PC. REJECTED: contradicts 30beab3 (itself a fix for a real race) and
   POWER_DOMAIN_EVALUATION.md:22,25.

Recommend A now (minimal, matches Phase 5's retention-is-a-no-op reality), B for
Phase 6 when the crossbar hazard must also close.

GPU compute unit (gpu_compute_unit.sv:227) asserts if_arvalid_o for exactly 1 cycle (drops when warp_busy set). Crossbar enters R_AR one cycle later, re-samples m_arvalid=0, SRAM never sees valid AR, crossbar stuck in R_AR, if_rvalid_i never returns, GPU never retires -> GPS_DONE never asserts. Not caught in Phase 4 (mock slave gave arready=1 same-cycle, crossbar not in path). Write engine g_wr_engine has same structural issue (W_AW re-samples m_awvalid) but latent: CPU D-cache holds awvalid stable per AXI4. Blocks bead 777 (SW coherency test) and likely ov2 (CPU-GPU integration). Test ready: tb/cocotb/soc/test_soc_coherency.py + coherency_fw/gen_coherency_hex.py, target soc_coherency.

title: RTL: CPU D-cache caches MMIO region — peripheral access broken at SoC level
description: M9 periph-loopback test (claude_verilog_test-k12) revealed: rv32i_core u_dcache (write-back, rv32i_core.sv:812) caches ALL dmem addresses with no uncached/device region. CPU firmware MMIO stores to 0x2000_xxxx peripheral ring are absorbed into dirty cache lines and NEVER reach the peripheral; status-register loads return a stale cached value. Proven in sim: DMA AXI-Lite ctrl slave write-valid count = 0 over 200k cycles; CPU spins forever polling DMA STATUS done bit. Blocks ALL CPU-firmware-driven peripheral control: DMA, UART, SPI, timer, IRQ ctrl, AND the future CPU->GPU kernel-launch fast-follow. FIX (architectural): add an uncached MMIO window (>=0x2000_0000 peripheral+debug region) decoded in the CPU dmem path so those accesses bypass the D-cache straight to AXI. Requires architecture decision + RTL. Delegate to chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator.

title: check-cdc-timing target cannot fail a build: OpenSTA exits 0 after internal error
description:
Found while fixing CodeRabbit findings on PR #133 (bead k07 follow-up).

pnr/scripts/check_cdc_timing.tcl reports unmatched CDC exceptions correctly
(CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS) and raises a Tcl 'error' at the end of read_sdc. BUT the
OpenSTA 'sta' process still returns EXIT CODE 0. Confirmed both before and after
the CodeRabbit fixes, so this is pre-existing OpenSTA/Tcl batch-mode behaviour,
not a regression.

Consequence: 'make check-cdc-timing-asap7-soc' is ADVISORY, not a gate. It prints
failures but cannot fail CI or a script. Anyone wiring it into an automated flow
and trusting the exit status would get a silent pass.

This matters for GH #96 (multi-clock ASAP7 PD re-closure), which is expected to
rely on this target to prove the CDC budgets are met post-route. If the exit code
is meaningless, #96 could 'pass' CDC timing closure without anything actually
being checked.

Fix options:
  (a) have check_cdc_timing.tcl accumulate a failure flag and call 'exit 1'
      explicitly at the end rather than relying on Tcl 'error' propagation;
  (b) wrap the sta invocation in pnr/Makefile so it greps the log for
      CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS and fails the make target on any hit;
  (c) both -- (a) for direct 'sta script.tcl' use, (b) as a belt-and-braces
      guard at the Makefile level.

Recommend (c). Note the same class of issue is why GH #95's cdc_gate.py exit
status is the verdict rather than cdc_snitch's own -- a check whose exit code
does not reflect its findings is not a gate.

PD change -> chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator. Do before/with GH #96.

title: cdc_reset_sync has no scan bypass - will block DFT scan insertion
description:
Found during GH #95 ARM/open-source CDC survey.

rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_reset_sync.sv drives its flop chain's asynchronous clear directly from
rst_n_i with no scan-mode override. During scan shift the reset must be controllable by
the tester, otherwise the synchroniser chain cannot be scanned and the whole CPU/fabric
reset tree becomes untestable.

OpenTitan's equivalent primitive (prim_rst_sync) muxes in scan_rst_ni under scanmode_i
for exactly this reason. Standard practice: every async-reset synchroniser in a
scan-inserted design needs a scan_rst_ni / scanmode_i pair (or a test_mode reset mux).

Affects both cdc_reset_sync instances in async_axi_fifo (u_s_rst_sync, u_m_rst_sync),
both in apb_cdc_bridge (u_s_rst_sync, u_m_rst_sync), and u_cpu_pmu_rst_sync in soc_top.

Not currently blocking: this project has no DFT/scan flow yet (chip-design-dft
orchestrator exists but has not been run on this design). Filing now because the fix is
cheap while the primitive has only ~5 instantiation sites, and expensive later.

RTL change -> chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator, coordinate with chip-design-dft.

title: Tighten gray-pointer set_max_delay to 0.5x period; split post-route CDC SDC (OpenTitan precedent)
description:
Two SDC refinements with strong primary-source precedent, for GH #96 PD re-closure.
Item 2 may invalidate GH #94's CDC budgets entirely -- raised to P2 for that reason.

== 2. SET_MAX_DELAY MAY BE MASKED BY SET_CLOCK_GROUPS -ASYNCHRONOUS (potentially serious) ==

phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc has BOTH set_clock_groups -asynchronous (line 105) and
set_max_delay -datapath_only (sections 11-13) in ONE file. Its own comment at lines
100-103 asserts:

  'those get explicit set_max_delay -datapath_only overrides in sections 11-13 below,
   which OpenSTA honours even though the clock groups are otherwise asynchronous.'

That claim is UNVERIFIED -- per CLAUDE.md the SDC 'is not yet run through OpenSTA'.
And standard SDC exception precedence is:
    set_false_path  >  set_max_delay / set_min_delay  >  set_multicycle_path
set_clock_groups -asynchronous creates false paths between the groups. False path
wins. So the max_delay constraints are likely being silently DROPPED, which would
make all of GH #94's CDC budgets decorative.

OpenTitan hit exactly this and solved it by SPLITTING the SDC. Their check-only file
(hw/top_earlgrey/syn/chip_earlgrey_asic_check_only.sdc) opens verbatim:

  'These SDC's are not used for synthesis, since they collide with the current
   set_clock_groups -async constraints. Instead, they are used to time the design
   after P&R in order to make sure that the CDC crossings are all within spec.'

ACTION: run the SDC through OpenSTA and report whether the max_delay paths are timed
or dropped. If dropped, split into phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc (implementation, keeps
set_clock_groups) + phase5_soc_multiclock_check.sdc (post-route CDC verification,
keeps set_max_delay), per OpenTitan. Also fix the incorrect comment either way.

== 1. TWO-TIER CDC BUDGET ==

Current SDC bounds every CDC path to one destination-clock period. Precedent is
stricter and two-tier:
  OpenTitan check_only.sdc:  0.9 x destination period for all crossings,
                             GRAY_MAX_DELAY = 0.5 x period for FIFO gray pointers
  PULP cdc_fifo_gray.sv:     set_max_delay min(T_src, T_dst) -- the MINIMUM of the
                             two periods, not the destination's
Our mem_q read at ~1.0x is looser than OpenTitan's data path; our gray pointers at
~1.0x are 2x looser than theirs. Recommend 0.5x on the 10 gray-pointer crossings
(2 per FIFO x 5 FIFOs in u_cpu_axi_cdc) and 0.9x on mem_q.

PD/SDC change -> chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator. Fold into GH #96.
close_reason: SDC split + budget tightening committed (8336853); see comment for tool-verified evidence

title: Port OpenTitan prim_cdc_rand_delay metastability injection into cdc_2ff_sync
description:
Closes the 'metastability injection is not modelable in Verilator' residual gap
recorded in design_state.json:164 and CLAUDE.md.

OpenTitan does model it. hw/ip/prim_generic/rtl/prim_flop_2sync.sv wraps its first
synchroniser stage in:

    `ifdef SIMULATION
      prim_cdc_rand_delay #(.DataWidth(Width), .Enable(EnablePrimCdcRand))
      u_prim_cdc_rand_delay (.clk_i, .rst_ni, .src_data_i(d_i),
                             .prev_data_i(intq), .dst_data_o(d_o));
    `else
      always_comb d_o = d_i;
    `endif

prim_cdc_rand_delay.sv is 67 lines of plain RTL (randomised delay model, not #delay),
so it IS portable to a Verilator flow -- which contradicts our current claim that
metastability is unmodelable here. Defeatable per-instance via the Enable parameter.

Would give real coverage of the class of bug GH #93 found only by accident at a
divergent clock ratio. Apply to rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_2ff_sync.sv (every synchroniser in
the design is an instance of it, so one edit covers all 13+ crossings).

Verilator lint waiver precedent also in OpenTitan: hw/ip/prim/lint/prim_cdc_rand_delay.vlt
lint_off UNUSED for the whole file.

RTL change -> chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator. Needs async_axi_fifo +
apb_cdc_bridge + soc_all re-run after.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION LANDED BUT IS DEFECTIVE — reopened, do not close.

The infrastructure is right: rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_2ff_sync.sv now carries an optional
randomised-delay injector, guarded by `ifdef SIMULATION (defined only by
tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile, never by lint_soc / tools/cdc / pnr sv2v), parameter
RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN defaulting OFF, seeded for reproducibility. Verified: lint clean,
CDC gate 0 unwaived with counts BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-change baseline
(OK1 17791 / CDC 39 / OKX 330 / BAD 16088), so the synthesis path really is unchanged.

THE MODEL IS WRONG. hold_sel is redrawn only inside `always @(d_i)`:

    always @(d_i) begin ... hold_sel = ($urandom_range(0,99) < RAND_CDC_DELAY_PCT); end
    assign stage0_d = hold_sel ? sync_q[0] : d_i;

If hold_sel latches 1 on a d_i transition, stage0_d becomes sync_q[0] — a self-loop.
sync_q[0] then never changes, and because d_i has already finished transitioning the
always block never fires again, so hold_sel stays 1. The synchroniser is STUCK-AT its
old value permanently. That is not 'one extra cycle of settling delay', it is a
functional break of the primitive.

EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED: forcing RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN=1 and running async_axi_fifo gives
TESTS=26 PASS=3 FAIL=23. The failures are the injector breaking the design, not the
injector finding design bugs.

This is why nothing in the repo opts in — the feature is dormant everywhere
(RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN=1 appears at zero instantiation sites), so as committed it delivers
exactly zero verification value while carrying the maintenance cost.

FIX NEEDED: redraw the hold decision once per DESTINATION CLOCK EDGE while
d_i != sync_q[0], not on d_i transitions. The natural form is to fold the decision into
the clocked stage-0 process (or an always @(posedge clk_i) helper), so a held cycle is
followed by another draw on the next edge and the value always converges. Compare
OpenTitan prim_cdc_rand_delay.sv, which takes both src_data_i AND prev_data_i and is
evaluated in the destination clock's process for exactly this reason.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (none of which were met):
  1. With RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN=1 forced at every site, async_axi_fifo and apb_cdc_bridge
     must still PASS — a correct synchroniser must tolerate extra settling delay. Any
     failure there is a real finding to be reported, not the expected outcome.
  2. Demonstrate it CATCHES something: deliberately break a synchroniser (e.g. revert
     the 7a9f9d4 wr_ready_o reset gating) and show the suite fails with the injector on
     and passes with it off.
  3. Then wire at least one CDC-focused suite to run with it enabled, otherwise the
     feature stays dormant and buys nothing.

title: apb_cdc_bridge 2-phase toggle is not one-sided-reset safe; PMU resets CPU domain alone
description:
Research finding (primary sources) + empirical result from GH #95 directed testing.

== STATUS: no counterexample found in simulation; class concern remains open ==

GH #95 added 3 directed one-sided-reset tests to test_apb_cdc_bridge.py
(test_reset_asym_s_held_m_free, test_reset_asym_staggered_s_then_m,
test_reset_asym_staggered_m_then_s), on top of pre-existing
test_reset_mid_transaction_m_side / test_availability_* coverage. Suite is 22/22 PASS.

Verified clean across stagger windows of 1x/3x/8x the slower period, both release
orders, at 7/13ns, 18/4ns and 10ns-equal ratios:
  - m_psel/m_penable never pulse while m_rst_n_i is genuinely low (no fabricated
    destination write)
  - s_pready always force-completes within bounded time (no hang)
  - post-recovery reads/writes land exactly once (no duplication)

IMPORTANT: this is empirical absence-of-failure in the constructed scenarios, NOT a
proof that the class is safe. cocotb cannot establish the general property. A formal
treatment would need chip-design-formal (2-phase toggle FSM reachability under
arbitrary one-sided reset timing). Leaving this bead OPEN on that basis.

== THE UNDERLYING CLASS CONCERN (unchanged) ==

Both PULP and OpenTitan independently conclude a 2-phase (NRZ) handshake CDC is
unsafe under one-sided asynchronous reset, and both ship a 4-phase (RZ) variant
specifically to fix it:

- PULP cdc_reset_ctrlr.sv: 'We use a 4-phase rather than a 2-phase CDC to avoid the
  issues of one-sided async reset that might trigger spurious transactions.'
- OpenTitan prim_sync_reqack.sv: the RZ four-phase option 'is safe to reset either
  domain in isolation, since the two FSMs cannot get out of sync due to persistent
  EVEN/ODD states.' Its NRZ default instead carries the contract 'When resetting one
  domain, also the other domain needs to be reset with both resets being active at
  the same time', machine-checked by SyncReqAckRstSrc/Dst assertions.

rtl/soc/apb_cdc_bridge.sv is 2-phase toggle -- the variant both projects call unsafe.
Today largely masked by cross-coupled resets, BUT the PMU can reset the CPU domain
alone (pmu_cpu_rst_n), which is exactly the one-sided case.

Note apb_cdc_bridge.sv:281-335 documents a separate reviewed exception for
m_rst_n_s availability-gating -- different concern, not this one.

Resolution options if a counterexample is ever found: RZ 4-phase conversion (halves
throughput, irrelevant on a config path), or a documented+asserted contract that PMU
CPU-domain reset must not overlap an in-flight APB_PLL2 transaction.
notes:
ARM/open-source survey (GH #95) found a NAMED UPSTREAM FIX and confirms we are the minority choice.

Three independent implementations of an async APB bridge all use 4-phase RZ, not our
2-phase NRZ toggle, and at least one states the reason in exactly our terms:

  - ARM cmsdk_ahb_to_apb_async.v -- 4-phase, per its own OVL assertion names
    ('Test 4 phase hande shaking - phase 1', 'Req rising edge should only take place
    when Ack is low'). Structure otherwise identical to ours: 2x 2-FF on the handshake
    only, payload passed unsynchronised and held stable by the handshake.
  - Hazard3 hazard3_apb_async_bridge -- 4-phase.
  - OpenDAP bridge -- 4-phase, stating: 'A NRZI toggle handshake ... can cause spurious
    bus accesses when only one side of the link is reset.'

That last sentence is this bead, verbatim, from an upstream project.

So: our bridge's STRUCTURE matches ARM's async APB bridge exactly; only the handshake
ENCODING differs, and ours is the one all three projects avoided. Conversion to 4-phase
RZ halves throughput, which is irrelevant on a config path (APB_PLL2).

Note ARM's STA guidance for its async bridge is the older set_false_path on the payload;
our GH #94 set_max_delay -datapath_only is the stronger choice.

title: PD port stubs missing cpu_clk_i/cpu_rst_n_i (blocks GH #96 multi-clock PD re-closure)

title: pmu.sv power-up ordering unsafe across async CPU domain (GH #90 follow-up)
description: Found during GH #93. pmu.sv's per-domain sequencer asserts rst_n_w=1 (DOM_PU_RST) one full core_clk cycle BEFORE it asserts clk_en_w=1 (DOM_PU_CLK) on the power-up path. Since GH #93, pmu_cpu_rst_n and pmu_cpu_clk_en cross into the independently-clocked cpu_core_clk domain through two SEPARATE 2-stage synchronisers, so the 1-cycle offset is not structurally preserved downstream. A live firmware-driven CPU power-down/up cycle could see cpu_domain_rst_n release before the clock ungates - the same bug class as 4398c2e, narrower window. Cold boot is unaffected (verified: soc_all 159/159). Fix likely in pmu.sv: merge DOM_PU_RST/DOM_PU_CLK, or ungate the clock before releasing reset. Note the UPF fixes the sequencing order, so check phase5_soc.upf compliance before changing it. Untested area: no suite exercises PMU-driven live power-cycling across domains.
notes: Fixed in rtl/soc/soc_top.sv (not pmu.sv -- UPF-mandated ordering preserved). Gated u_cpu_cg enable with pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync: cpu_gated_clk_en = ~pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync. Verified lint_soc 0 errors, make pmu 10/10, soc_boot 3/3 (100/100 stability), soc_multiclock 4/4. Commit on feat/cpu-domain-cdc-gh93.

title: Sky130 SoC Stage-2: setup fails at ss corner (WNS -8.9ns); sign-off gated to tt only
description:
Found 2026-07-28 auditing run RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57. At 65 MHz (CLOCK_PERIOD 15.385 ns) the SoC closes setup at tt and ff but FAILS at all three ss corners: max_ss_100C_1v60 WNS -8.902 ns / TNS -118.16 ns; nom_ss -7.767; min_ss -6.386. Checker.SetupViolations reports 'No setup violations found' ONLY because pnr/sky130/soc/config.json sets TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS=['*tt*'] — STA_CORNERS runs all 9, but the gate ignores ss and ff. So the 'Stage-2 signed off at 65 MHz' claim is tt-only and should be stated that way.

ROOT CAUSE: the CPU hard macro's characterized clk->Q. Worst ss path is u_cpu/clk_i -> u_cpu/axi_araddr_o[15] = 8.155 ns, i.e. 53% of the 15.385 ns period consumed inside the macro before any SoC logic runs. The 12 worst ss paths are all u_cpu -> u_cpu or *_ -> u_cpu. This is bead 1ls (GH #123) resurfacing at the slow corner: 4.55 ns clk->Q at nom_tt, 7.54 at nom_ss, 8.12 at max_ss, against a 2.0 ns set_output_delay budget in pnr/sky130/cpu/constraints/sky130_cpu.sdc that gives the optimizer no pressure.

CONTEXT: 1ls was closed 2026-07-25 with 'Accepted 65 MHz (user decision)' after proving budget tightening is a dead end (8.0 ns budget failed to close Stage-1: WNS -2.950, 4826 hold endpoints). That decision was about not reaching 75 MHz — it did NOT establish that ss fails outright at 65 MHz. This bead records that distinct fact so it is not lost.

OPTIONS: (a) document the tt-only position explicitly and keep 65 MHz — cheapest, but then Sky130 Stage-2 is not a true multi-corner sign-off; (b) drop the SoC clock to ~41 MHz (1/(15.385+8.902)) so ss closes honestly; (c) re-harden the Stage-1 CPU macro against an ss-aware budget — 1ls suggests this is very hard for this topology. NOTE the ss numbers are honest for the CPU macro (9 per-corner CPU libs staged 2026-07-25, commit 86e89c1) but the SRAM macro is still TT-only analytical (bead o1i / GH #120), so the ss result carries some SRAM-model error. DECISION NEEDED — not PD tuning.
notes:
2026-07-29 RESULT — the 40 MHz relaxation did NOT close ss. RUN_2026-07-29_18-40-38 post-PnR STA at CLOCK_PERIOD 25.0 ns: max_ss setup WNS -4.328 ns (was -8.902 @15.385), nom_ss -2.885, min_ss -1.120. tt and ff clean.

WHY THE 41 MHz ESTIMATE WAS WRONG: it assumed path delay is invariant under relaxation. It is not. Effective path was 24.287 ns at T=15.385 and 29.328 ns at T=25.0 — 5.041 ns slower for 9.615 ns of relaxation, i.e. dpath/dT = 0.524. Each ns of period buys only ~0.48 ns of slack because the optimizer hands speed back (downsizes cells) as soon as it has margin. Linear two-point fit: slack = 0.476*T - 16.222, zero at T = 34.08 ns = 29.3 MHz. Crude extrapolation from two points — the same give-back effect may recur, so 29 MHz is a lower bound on the answer, not a guarantee.

PARKED. User decision 2026-07-29: fix the hold regression first (see 9t6/58q), then re-judge frequency against a clean baseline. CLOCK_PERIOD stays at 25.0 ns meanwhile. Do not chase ss further until hold is green at all 9 corners.

title: PLL safety: clearing pll_enable (CONTROL[0]) self-bricks the SoC
description: CodeRabbit (PR #88) MAJOR, pre-existing (not introduced by the pll_subsystem refactor; same gating in old pll_axil_regs). pll_enable=CONTROL[0] in pll_apb_regs (clk_i domain, reset default=1). If firmware clears it: pll_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_enable->0 -> PLL held in reset -> pll_locked->0 -> core_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_locked->0 -> resets CPU+soc_bus. pll_apb_regs is NOT reset by core_rst_n (clk_i domain) so pll_enable stays 0 -> permanent deadlock; the APB master that wrote 0 is gone before it can write 1 back. FIX OPTIONS: (a) make CONTROL[0] set-only / non-clearable in SoC integration (firmware can enable, not disable); or (b) gate PLL reconfig so it doesn't drop core_rst_n in a non-recoverable way; or (c) add a startup/watchdog recovery. Functional design change -> own PR + soc_all re-verify. Natural to fold into #4 (3-PLL/CDC) where PLL control is reworked. NOT fixed in the refactor PR #88 (which preserved existing behavior).

title: SPI MISO sampled without 2-FF synchroniser (CDC hygiene)

title: Sky130 CPU Stage-1: Magic DRC reports 27.7M li.3 violations — never passed, likely LEF-abstract artifact
description: Every Sky130 Stage-1 CPU run reports Magic DRC errors: 27733913 — BIT-IDENTICAL between RUN_2026-07-21_18-02-11 and RUN_2026-07-27_05-52-19, so it is systematic and deterministic, not caused by any recent change. KLayout DRC on the same runs is 0 and Netgen LVS says 'Circuits match uniquely', which makes the Magic result the odd one out. The report (*-magic-drc/reports/drc_violations.magic.rpt, 27.7M lines) is dominated by 'Local interconnect spacing < 0.17um (li.3)' with roughly a dozen other rule types present (licon.1, licon.5a, licon.8, licon.8a, poly.2/4/7/8, psd.10b, nwell.4). PRIME SUSPECT: pnr/sky130/cpu/config.json sets MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: false, so Magic runs DRC on the LEF/DEF-derived view where the sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 macro is an abstract black box rather than real GDS geometry — a classic source of spurious li spacing errors at macro boundaries. Worth testing MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: true on one run to confirm before treating any of these as real. CONSEQUENCE: Stage-1 CPU has never had a genuine Magic DRC sign-off, and that gap is inherited by everything consuming the rv32i_cpu_top macro.

title: GH #123: CPU macro clk->Q on AXI outputs 4.55ns @nom_tt -- Stage-1 output budget far too loose
description: CORRECTED 2026-07-25 (original premise was wrong). pnr/sky130/cpu/constraints/sky130_cpu.sdc DOES budget I/O: 28 set_input_delay + 38 set_output_delay lines, 2.0ns max each side on the AXI ports. Real root cause is that the budget is TOO LOOSE: set_output_delay -max 2.0 against a 13.333ns period lets the macro take up to 11.33ns to produce an output; it takes 4.55ns @nom_tt (7.54 @nom_ss, 8.12 @max_ss) so the optimizer had zero pressure to do better. 4.55ns clk->Q at the TYPICAL corner is ~30% of the period gone before the signal leaves the macro. Second independent cause: rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:580-585 early-accept makes arready a combinational function of araddr via decode() + priority arbitration (the 7-gate fabric cone in the worst path). FIX: raise set_output_delay/set_input_delay on AXI ports so the macro must drive outputs in ~4-5ns, re-run librelane-sky130-cpu, confirm it still closes at 13.333ns and clk->Q drops, re-stage 9 corner libs + LEF/GDS, re-run Stage-2 at 75MHz. Only if insufficient, consider registering crossbar arready (costs 1 cycle/read, needs decision + full re-verification).
notes: GitHub issue #123. NEGATIVE RESULT 2026-07-25: budget tightening CANNOT recover 75MHz. Tried 2.0->8.0ns on AXI ports (RUN_2026-07-25_19-30-52): Stage-1 failed to close, setup WNS -2.950 on apb_prdata_o[13] (APB budget untouched -- the AXI tightening ate design-wide optimizer headroom), 4826 hold-violating endpoints. Reboot killed it at 19:48 but it had already failed. MATH: need 2.052ns; have 0.241 slack; must recover 1.811ns from macro; requires clk->Q 4.545->2.734ns (40% cut) = 10.6ns budget, MORE aggressive than the 8.0 that failed. No viable value exists. SDC REVERTED to 2.0ns. REAL TARGET: crossbar fabric = 8.83ns of the nom_tt path (20 driver stages) vs macro 4.55ns -- the araddr->decode->arbitration->arready early-accept cone at rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:580-585. Options now: (1) register crossbar arready, costs 1 cycle/read + full re-verif; (2) pipeline decode; (3) accept 65MHz. Design decision, not PD tuning.
close_reason: Accepted 65 MHz (user decision 2026-07-25). Budget tightening proven a dead end: 8.0ns failed to close (WNS -2.950, 4826 hold endpoints); 75MHz would need 10.6ns, more aggressive still. SDC reverted to 2.0ns. Real target is the crossbar early-accept cone (fabric 8.83ns vs macro 4.55ns on the nom_tt path, rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:580-585) but both fixes trade read latency against verified RTL and Sky130 caps this topology at ~100-120MHz anyway. title: GH #120: SPICE-characterize sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 at ss/ff corners (CPU macro DONE)
description:
SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-01: this issue is now SRAM-ONLY. The CPU macro half of the original description is obsolete -- see 'Historical' at the end.

The SoC's SRAM hard macro sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 (OpenRAM compile) provides only a single characterized Liberty view: TT_1p8V_25C. pnr/sky130/soc/config.json's MACROS entry deliberately maps that one .lib to every PVT corner via a wildcard ("lib": {"*": [...]}), so the macro's internal timing arcs are IDENTICAL in all nine reported corners. Only sky130_fd_sc_hd standard cells, and the CPU macro, genuinely vary by corner in this flow.

Consequence (bidirectional -- and note the direction was guessed WRONG once already, see below):
- nom_tt results are valid: the one corner where this macro's characterization matches the analysis label.
- ss/ff results on paths touching the SRAM macro boundary carry macro-model error of UNKNOWN SIGN. Do not assume it is conservative. When the CPU macro was given genuine per-corner libs on 2026-07-25, the earlier reasoning that ss HOLD was 'pessimistic and plausibly fine in real silicon' proved wrong: max_ss hold went -0.0708 -> -0.3997 ns and nom_tt hold went from MET to VIOLATING. The wildcard was optimistic in BOTH directions, not offsetting.
- Therefore Sky130 SoC Stage-2 timing is a TYPICAL-CORNER (nom_tt) SIGN-OFF, not a validated multi-corner one, despite reporting numbers under ss/ff corner labels. The physical gates (Netgen LVS PASSED, routing DRC 0, PDN 0, KLayout DRC 4 waived) are NOT affected by this and stand as real results.

This macro is the SOLE remaining source of that limitation.

Fix (the only remaining one): characterize sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 at ss/ff for real. OpenRAM supports multi-corner characterization natively (process_corners / supply_voltages / temperatures, nominal_corner_only=False); our compile used nominal_corner_only=True for speed during the views-first pass. Doing it properly needs SPICE-based characterization per corner -- NOT the analytical mode, which is separately known-broken for power (it emitted internal_power ~1.99e11 mW, currently hand-zeroed in the staged .lib).

STATUS: DEFERRED host-blocked. See the feasibility verdict in NOTES -- ~26-31 h/corner, ~80-95 h total, measured from Xyce's own progress meter, against a host that reboots every 2-8 h. Not a tuning problem; no amount of PD iteration substitutes for it. Bead ujv (Stage-2 ss setup failure) is deferred for the same underlying reason and cannot be honestly closed before this one is.

Keep the two documented hand-patches on the TT lib (zeroed internal_power; max_transition 0.04 -> 0.5, required because 40 ps is unachievable in sky130_fd_sc_hd and OpenROAD hard-aborts with RSZ-0090). Revisit only with a machine that stays up ~4 days, or with a genuinely reduced characterization netlist.

Related: separate from claude_verilog_test-0jp (the 4 KLayout DRC violations, closed won't-fix), though both stem from the same views-first macro-compile pattern.

--- Historical (superseded 2026-07-25, retained for provenance) ---
The original description asserted that BOTH hard macros (rv32i_cpu_top and the SRAM) had only a single nom_tt Liberty view, and prescribed re-running the Stage-1 CPU characterization flow as part of the fix. That is no longer true. rv32i_cpu_top was fixed on 2026-07-25: config.json now maps 9 exact corner keys to 9 genuinely distinct per-corner Liberty views in pnr/sky130/cpu/macro/, verified from each corner's own sta.log. Those views had in fact always existed -- Stage-1's OpenROAD.STAPostPNR wrote all nine; only nom_tt had ever been staged into the SoC config, which then wildcarded it across every corner.
notes: 2026-07-27 FEASIBILITY VERDICT: NOT FEASIBLE on this host, measured not estimated. Xyce's own progress meter in temp_charretry/spice_stdout.log: 'Percent complete: 17.0783 %' at 05:37:07 with 'Estimated time to completion: 52 min., 33 sec.' => ONE delay simulation ~63 minutes. OpenRAM does NOT run one simulation per corner: delay.py find_feasible_period_one_port is a period-doubling loop capped at 9 iterations (time_out=9), then find_min_period_one_port runs a BINARY SEARCH, repeated per read port -- this macro has 2 read ports (1RW+1R). That is roughly 25-30 full simulations per corner = ~26-31 h/corner, ~80-95 h for the 3 corners, against a host that reboots every 2-8 h and where tmux does not survive. The netlist-only sram_char.py path (which removed the 3.7 h routing per attempt) does not help: the cost is the SPICE search itself. Note sram_char.py forces trim_netlist=False, and the 'trimmed.sp' from the generation run is 4.30 MB vs the full 4.17 MB sram.sp -- trimming is not meaningfully shrinking this 32768-bit array, so there is no easy speedup there. The 05:17 run also died at 17% for an unexplained reason (no kernel OOM in journalctl -k, no systemd-oomd entry, no Python traceback, timing.raw had reached 1.0 GB); that is unresolved but MOOT -- even a clean run cannot fit the search into this host's uptime. RECOMMENDATION: keep both documented hand-patches on the TT lib (zeroed internal_power, max_transition 0.04->0.5), leave the macro analytical + single-corner, and pursue bead 0ro instead. Revisit only with a machine that stays up ~4 days or with a genuinely trimmed/reduced characterization netlist.
